title: All three savings products share one vault implementation and one set of role addresses, correlating their failure modes
content:
The Spark Savings instances repeat four addresses verbatim: `Spark Vault v2 Implementation` `0x1b992302...`, `Default admin` `0x3300f198...`, `Setter` `0x2E1b01ad...` and `Taker` `0x1601843c...` appear identically under ETH (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.9.1.4.1.1–.4), USDC (.9.2.4.1.1–.4) and USDT (.9.3.4.1.1–.4). The Morpho instances show the same convergence on the venue side: one `Curator Role Address` `0x0f963A8A...` and one `Guardian Role Address` `0xf5748bBe...` across Morpho Dai, USDS, USDC and the Blue Chip USDT Vault, with the Allocator shared by three of the four.

Documenting each instance independently makes them look like independent risks. Reading the addresses shows they are not. A defect in the shared vault implementation is a defect in every savings product simultaneously; compromise of the Setter key moves every published rate; compromise of the Taker key sweeps all three deposit bases at once — and those operations, as documented, carry no rate limit.

The same holds for the third-party side: one curator's judgement governs Spark's position across four Morpho vaults, so 'diversifying across Morpho vaults' provides less independence than the instance count suggests.

Sharing an implementation is normal and desirable — one audited contract is safer than three variants. The point is that the per-instance document structure systematically hides correlation, and the only way to see it is to compare address values across siblings. Risk assessed instance-by-instance, as the Artifact's organisation invites, will overstate how independent these exposures are.
